newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 28.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- The government will seize an estimated 339 billion worth of assests from Chung Tai-soo, founder of the failed Hanbo Group, and his family, and Chung's third son and chairman of Hanbo Group, Chung Bo-keun, is expected to be arrested on Friday.
- Deputy Finance Minister Kang Man-soo said on Thursday that the Korean economy faced a temporary and manageable disturbance, but not a crisis.

- The Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency(KOTRA) said on Thursday it plans to send an official to North Korea tomorrow to discuss ways to set up its trade office at the North's special economic zone.
- President Kim Young-sam is likely to meet with opposition leaders Kim Dae jung and Kim Jong-pil next week to discuss ways to overcome the current economic crisis.
- In accordance with its long-term corporate strategy of "selective concentration" the LG Group plans to discard up to 90 marginal business lines by 2000.
- A bus plunged into a river in the southern city of Pusan--four dead and one person still missing.
